title: Vertical charge-coupled columns replace per-bit access transistors
idea: Substitute the per-cell access transistor with CCD-style transfer gates: each 4F² footprint hosts a vertical column of 16-32 potential wells (one per tier, formed by tier gate-planes wrapped around a shared single-crystal Si pillar), and a 3-phase clock shifts the column's charge packets up to one sense node at the top and writes them back down. Only that top node needs a transistor and contact.
why: Attacks fact 2 (lateral transistor blocks 3D DRAM) and per-tier contact count: N bits per 4F² with 1/N the transistors, ~8-10x bits/footprint at 32 tiers; column access ~20-40 ns suits page/stream tiers.

title: Interdigitating nano-comb bond splits one capacitor across two wafers
idea: Substitute one AR-115 capacitor etch with two AR-40 etches: wafer A carries storage-node pillars, wafer B carries matching holes lined with ZrO2 and the plate electrode; face-to-face hybrid bonding with ~10 nm overlay slides pillars into holes, producing a capacitor whose electrode length is the sum of both.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): Cs ~5->9 fF with no etch above 40:1, each etch cheaper and higher-yield; plate wafer moves off the critical path.

title: Strain-release rolls planar arrays into vertical Swiss-roll micro-tubes
idea: Substitute deposited tiers with rolled turns: build a planar thin-film array (oxide-semiconductor 2T0C cells plus wiring) on a strained SiNx/SiNx bilayer over a sacrificial Ge layer; release makes the membrane self-roll into a 10-20-turn tube standing on edge contacts, so one planar litho flow yields 10-20 effective tiers per footprint.
why: 3D bit density without a 26+ tier deposition/etch stack (fact 2) or high-AR etch; capex per bit near a planar thin-film line; ~5-10x bits per footprint for capacity memory.

title: Arrays on both wafer faces share one sandwiched periphery layer
idea: Substitute the dead silicon bulk with a second array: build the 1T1C array and periphery on the front, bond to carrier, thin to ~1 um, then build a second low-temperature oxide-semiconductor 1T1C array on the backside (backside-power-delivery style) wired through ~100 nm nano-TSVs so both arrays share the same sense amps and decoders.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): sharing it across two arrays gives ~1.6-1.8x bits per wafer for one CMOS layer, reusing backside tools logic fabs are already buying.

title: Grounded shield pillars between vertical wordlines trade area for hammer immunity
idea: In vertical-wordline 3D DRAM, substitute every other wordline pillar with a grounded shield pillar etched in the same hole step and tied to the common plate, so no active wordline has an active neighbor; the lost area is bought back with ~30% more tiers, which is cheaper than area in 3D.
why: Row hammer (fact 9): coupling and electron-migration paths terminate on a fixed-potential conductor, expected threshold 1k -> >100k activations, removing TRR/RFM refresh overhead (part of fact 3's 10-20% bandwidth tax).

title: Vertical tier-column pages replace 8 kb horizontal rows
idea: Substitute the horizontal row as the unit of activation with a vertical slice: one activation opens N tiers x a 16-bitline group (e.g., 32x16 = 512 bits, one 64 B line); tier-select lines act as the row address and the vertical bitline pillar group is the page, each pillar landing on its own sense amp in a bonded CMOS wafer.
why: Destructive read and 128x overfetch (fact 8): 8 kb -> 512 b page cuts activation energy ~10x toward ~0.6 pJ per useful bit; activations spread over many small pages dilute hammer counts.

title: Gen-8.5 display glass replaces 300 mm wafers for capacity memory
idea: Substitute DRAM fabs with idle LCD/OLED backplane lines: use their IGZO TFT process on 2.2x2.5 m glass to build 4-8 stacked layers of relaxed-pitch (~0.8 um) oxide-semiconductor gain-cell arrays, dice into large memory tiles with a bonded small CMOS controller, and sell as CXL far-memory modules.
why: Capital intensity and EUV (fact 4): depreciated display capex, zero EUV, new supply outside the DRAM-fab bottleneck; ~30-50 GB per layer per panel, roughly $8-15/GB at 4-8 layers, competitive at today's 4x prices for a slower ~100-300 ns tier.

title: Cast or reclaimed silicon replaces prime CZ wafers under BEOL arrays
idea: When the array is built in BEOL-temperature tiers and the periphery is bonded from another wafer, the array wafer's substrate is only a flat carrier: substitute prime CZ silicon with reclaimed wafers, cast multicrystalline silicon (lower-purity Si3N4-coated crucibles, not Spruce-Pine-grade liners) or glass carriers.
why: Quartz-crucible chokepoint (Spruce Pine >80%): roughly halves prime-wafer demand per bit for bonded array/periphery products and cuts substrate cost ~$50-100 per wafer.

title: Hexagonal 60-degree lattice replaces square grid for vertical-channel cells
idea: Substitute the orthogonal wordline/bitline grid with a triangular lattice: vertical-channel transistors at hexagonal close-packed sites defined by block-copolymer self-assembly, wordlines along one lattice direction and bitlines along a second at 60 degrees, so each cell occupies sqrt(3)/2*(2F)² = 3.46F² instead of 4F².
why: Litho-bound density (fact 4): ~13% more bits per area at the same F, a free 'half-node' without a new litho tool; hexagonal pillars also match the existing capacitor honeycomb.

title: Spare-wafer remapping replaces known-good-die testing in wafer-on-wafer stacks
idea: Substitute die-level HBM stacking (TSV + microbump + known-good-die test) with wafer-on-wafer hybrid bonding of 9 full DRAM wafers, one a spare; every bank has a fuse-programmable vertical bypass in the base logic so a failed bank on tier k is remapped to the same footprint on the spare tier.
why: HBM TSV tax and 20-30% yield loss (fact 6): one bond step per wafer instead of per die; stack yield rises from ~0.92^8 = 51% to >85% for 12.5% area overhead.

title: Array-only DRAM fab plus U.S. mature-node periphery foundry, hybrid-bonded
idea: Substitute the monolithic DRAM die with a two-wafer product: the DRAM fab makes an array-only wafer (cells, bitlines, WL straps, ~40% fewer masks) and an existing U.S. 28-40 nm logic fab makes a periphery-only wafer (sense amps, decoders, I/O) with sub-array-edge pads at ~1 um pitch; the two are hybrid-bonded.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): ~1.8x bits per DRAM-fab wafer, better periphery transistors, and half of each chip made in U.S. fabs that already exist.

title: Gain-cell shadow-row tier replaces the sense-amp latch as row buffer
idea: Substitute the single sense-amp row buffer per bank with an extra top tier of nondestructive 3T oxide-semiconductor gain cells over each sub-array holding 8-16 'shadow rows'; an activated row is copied once into a shadow, and later hits and re-opens read the shadow without re-activating or re-restoring the DRAM row.
why: Destructive read (fact 8) and row hammer (fact 9): est. 3-5x fewer activations on server traces, cutting ACT energy and aggressor counts; the tier is stacked, not added to footprint (~5% cost).

title: Coaxial grounded sleeve around vertical bitlines replaces bare pillars
idea: In vertical-bitline 3D DRAM, substitute the bare bitline pillar with a coax: ALD grounded TiN sleeve / Al2O3 / inner bitline, the sleeve opened only at each tier's access-transistor window by a self-aligned lateral recess, converting BL-to-BL coupling into fixed ground capacitance.
why: Neighbor-coupling noise caps tiers per sense amp in VBL designs; shielding allows ~2x more tiers per SA (taller pillars), roughly halving SA count (periphery, fact 7).

title: Transferred 2D-crystal tiers replace deposited semiconductor tiers
idea: Substitute epitaxial/deposited tier stacks with wafer-scale dry transfer of MOCVD monolayer MoS2 channels plus hBN gate dielectric grown on reusable sapphire donors, stacked tier by tier with a non-fluorinated polymer handle (PPC); each cell tier including its gate is <10 nm thick.
why: Tier pitch ~60+ nm (Si/SiGe) -> ~20-30 nm, 2-3x more tiers per um of stack and lower slit/hole AR (fact 2); 1.8 eV channel pushes leakage orders of magnitude below the 13 fA tail (fact 3).

title: Per-tier pulsed plates replace the static half-VDD common plate
idea: Substitute the global static plate at VARY/2 with tier-segmented plates driven by periphery: during restore the plate is pulsed -0.5 V so a 0.6 V bitline swing stores today's 1.1 V-equivalent charge, and during read it is bumped to boost signal into the SA; in 3D each tier's plate is naturally a separate film.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): VARY ~1.0 -> 0.6 V cuts array CV² energy ~2.5x and lowers wordline boost (~3 -> 2.4 V).

title: Mass-transfer printing of pre-tested micro-tiles replaces monolithic stacking
idea: Substitute TSV die stacks or monolithic tiers with microLED-style elastomer-stamp mass transfer: 60x60 um DRAM sub-array micro-tiles (array + local SAs, ~3 um thick, released by sacrificial undercut) are tested on the source wafer and printed layer by layer onto a logic host with planarized redistribution vias between layers.
why: Yield and data movement (facts 5-6): bad tiles discarded at 60 um granularity instead of whole dies; memory sits within um of compute; tool base already exists in microLED fabs.

title: Smart-cut silicon carbide tier replaces silicon access transistors
idea: Substitute the silicon access-transistor layer with a ~200 nm 4H-SiC layer transferred from a reusable SiC donor (as SmartSiC does for power devices) and bonded over the capacitor array; 3.26 eV bandgap and ~1e-9 cm^-3 intrinsic carrier density (vs 1e10 in Si) suppress junction/GIDL leakage, while low mobility is irrelevant for an access device.
why: Leakage tail forces refresh (fact 3): retention 64 ms -> seconds-minutes, cutting refresh power (16-33% of idle) and the 10-20% bandwidth loss by ~95%.

title: Wafer-scale DRAM bonded under a wafer-scale accelerator replaces HBM
idea: Substitute HBM stacks plus interposer with one full DRAM wafer hybrid-bonded face-to-face to a wafer-scale processor: each compute tile gets the DRAM directly beneath it through ~2 um-pitch bonds, and defective DRAM tiles are routed around by the processor's existing redundancy fabric.
why: Data-movement energy (fact 5): ~3-4 pJ/bit -> <0.3 pJ/bit and >10x bandwidth per mm², with no TSVs (fact 6) and no reticle-limited interposer.

title: Edge-standing bookshelf die stacks replace TSV vertical stacking
idea: Substitute horizontal TSV stacking with dies standing on edge like books: each thinned 30 um DRAM die routes I/O along its face to fine-pitch edge pads (exposed by dicing through scribe Cu bars), and 32-64 dies are laminated and bonded edge-down onto the base logic die, with heat leaving through full die faces to a top cold plate.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): no TSVs, so no 3x area per bit or via yield loss; ~1-2k edge pads per die at 10 um pitch supports HBM-class width.

title: Backside-etched capacitors in the thinned bulk replace front-side cylinders
idea: Substitute the front-side capacitor stack with capacitors etched from the wafer backside: after front-end transistors and bitlines, bond face-down, thin to ~3 um and etch capacitor holes from the back into silicon directly beneath each access transistor's storage junction, then line with ALD dielectric/electrode.
why: Capacitor charge wall and layout (facts 1, 4): the capacitor no longer competes with bitline/contacts for front area, can use the full 4F² footprint (~1.5x cross-section), and frees the BEOL; Cs ~7-8 fF at today's AR.

title: Retune idle 3D NAND lines into quasi-volatile charge-trap DRAM
idea: Substitute NAND's ~5 nm FN-programmed tunnel oxide with a ~1.5-2 nm direct-tunneling oxide in a 3D NOR-organized charge-trap stack: writes in ~10-50 ns at <4 V, retention seconds-hours (refreshed), low-field tunneling for very high endurance, on existing 200+ layer NAND tools with mask changes only.
why: Capital and supply (fact 4): converts underused 3D-stacking capex into DRAM-class capacity with ~5-10x fewer refreshes and NAND-like cost per bit.

title: Sawtooth multilayer mold replaces smooth capacitor cylinder walls
idea: Substitute the uniform oxide capacitor mold with a 10 nm-period SiO2/SiN nanolaminate; after the hole etch, recess SiN laterally ~5 nm in hot phosphoric acid so the ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN conforms to a sawtooth sidewall with ~1.7x surface area, a deterministic successor to 1990s hemispherical-grain poly.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): Cs 5 -> 8 fF at today's 60:1 AR, equivalent to AR ~100 without the harder etch; corrugations stiffen pillars against leaning.

title: Tier address encoded in epitaxial doping replaces 3D staircase contacts
idea: Substitute the staircase (one contact landing per tier) with a vertical decoder: each tier's select transistors are grown with an in-situ doping (thus Vt) set by its binary tier address, and ten vertical gate pillars (true/complement for 5 address bits) pass through all 32 tiers, so an address code turns on the series select chain of exactly one tier, like a NAND decoder.
why: 3D DRAM tier access (fact 2): removes staircase area (~5-10% of die) and its N trim/etch cycles; per-tier doping comes free during stack growth.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores replace fluorocarbon-etched capacitor molds
idea: Substitute fluorocarbon-etched oxide molds with anodic aluminum oxide: sputter 3-5 um Al over storage pads, two-step anodize in oxalic/phosphoric acid to grow 25-35 nm hexagonal pores at AR >100:1, open the barrier by phosphoric-acid widening, fill with TiCl4-based ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN; pore diameter < inter-pad gap so no pore bridges two cells and each pad statistically lands several pores in parallel.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): AR 100-150 at bath-tool cost gives Cs ~8-12 fF with zero C4F6/C4F8 etch, no mold litho, abundant aluminum.

title: Thermally drawn nanochannel glass slices replace etched capacitor holes
idea: Substitute etched holes with drawn glass: bundle acid-soluble core rods in an acid-resistant matrix glass, redraw 3-4 times to 30-50 nm channels (microchannel-plate style), fuse, saw into 10-20 um slices, leach cores in HCl, CMP with silica/KOH slurry, ALD electrodes, and oxide-bond the slice onto the transistor wafer using the channel-smaller-than-pad-gap landing rule.
why: Capacitor charge wall: AR set by slice thickness (300-500:1 possible) -> Cs >15 fF or smaller cells; capital shifts from EUV/HAR etch to glass draw towers, fully fluorine-free.

title: Epitaxial superlattice edges replace EUV for wordline pitch definition
idea: Substitute EUV/SAQP for the densest line layers with superlattice nanowire pattern transfer: grow a 512-period Si/Si0.7Ge0.3 superlattice (6/6 nm), cleave and polish its edge, recess SiGe with peracetic-acid etchant, evaporate Mo at glancing angle onto the Si ridges, and stamp the 512-wire, 12 nm-pitch array onto the target wafer, one stamp per sub-array mat.
why: Litho-bound scaling (fact 4): pitch set by epitaxy (+/-0.3 nm) not a scanner, deleting several EUV/SAQP passes per WL/BL layer while avoiding fluorinated resists and spacer etches.

title: All-epitaxial Si/SiGe stack etched only with HBr/Cl2 chemistry
idea: Substitute the oxide/nitride stack of 3D DRAM (etched with C4F6/C4F8/CH2F2) with an all-semiconductor Si/SiGe epitaxial stack whose slits and holes are etched only with HBr/Cl2/O2 at cryogenic chuck temperature (SiOxBry sidewall passivation), deferring every dielectric to non-fluorinated fills (aminosilane ALD SiO2, TMA Al2O3) planarized by CMP instead of etch-back.
why: Builds the 26-100 tier stacks 3D DRAM needs (fact 2) without fluorocarbon gases (GWP up to ~9,000) or their abatement, keeping single-crystal channels for a tight leakage tail.

title: Burn-out amorphous-carbon tiers replace nitride sacrificial layers in 3D
idea: Substitute sacrificial nitride/oxide tiers with PECVD amorphous-carbon tiers alternating with Si or IGZO channel tiers: cut slits with Cl2 (channel) and O2 (carbon), keep support pillars every ~2 um, then laterally ash the carbon with remote O2/H2 plasma (selectivity >1000:1) to open horizontal cavities for lateral capacitors.
why: Solves the lateral-capacitor cavity step of 3D DRAM (fact 2) with a dry release needing no HF or NF3; propylene-derived carbon is cheap and non-scarce.

title: Molybdenum from oxychloride replaces WF6 tungsten in 3D wordlines
idea: Substitute WF6-CVD tungsten in replacement-gate wordlines, staircase contacts and buried wordlines with molybdenum deposited from MoO2Cl2 (or MoCl5) + H2, which nucleates barrier-free on Al2O3/SiO2 so the TiN glue layer is dropped and more of each 15-20 nm tier cavity is conductor.
why: Removes fluorine (WF6 releases HF that attacks high-k) and tungsten (China ~80%) at once; ~30-40% lower line resistance in narrow tiers allows longer wordlines and fewer drivers (fact 7).

title: Argon fast-atom activated Si-Si bonding replaces HF-last tier bonding
idea: Substitute HF-dip hydrophobic bonding and oxide-interface bonding with room-temperature surface-activated bonding: an Ar fast-atom beam in UHV strips the native oxide and two single-crystal Si tiers are pressed into a conductive, oxide-free junction, so vertical bitline/channel pillars run continuously through layer-transferred tiers.
why: Monolithic-quality 3D tiers (fact 2) with dry, fluorine-free surface prep; conductive bonds remove one via per tier per pillar (~10-20% fewer steps per tier).

title: Molecular monolayer doping replaces BF3/PF3 implants on 3D sidewalls
idea: Substitute beamline BF3/PF3/GeF4 implants (which cannot reach 100-tier hole sidewalls anyway) with monolayer doping: self-assembled allylboronic-acid-pinacol-ester or diethyl-vinylphosphonate monolayers coat every exposed Si sidewall, are capped with ALD oxide, and spike-annealed into ~5 nm conformal junctions on all tiers at once.
why: Dopes 3D DRAM lateral access transistors on every tier in one step (fact 2) without fluorinated dopant gases; abrupt shallow junctions cut GIDL, the leakage-tail driver (fact 3).

title: Fluorine-free-release nanoimprint replaces EUV on periodic array layers
idea: Substitute EUV exposures of the strictly periodic array layers (active, buried WL, BL, landing pad) with jet-and-flash nanoimprint, replacing the fluorinated anti-stick template silane (FDTS/FOTS) with a self-releasing siloxane-methacrylate resist plus a renewable water-soluble PVA release film and radical (PAG-free) UV cure.
why: EUV is one supplier and DRAM needs 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4): NIL is ~1/3-1/5 the capex per layer, buildable in the U.S., and the PFAS-free release removes NIL's own fluorine dependence.

title: Infiltrated block-copolymer dots replace EUV pillar-hole patterning
idea: Substitute EUV contact/pillar patterning with self-assembly: PS-b-P2VP cylinders form a hexagonal lattice at 20-28 nm pitch inside coarse ArF-dry guide trenches, 3 cycles of sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O) turn P2VP domains into AlOx hard-mask dots, PS is O2-ashed and the pattern transferred with Cl2/HBr.
why: Litho capital (fact 4): sub-20 nm dense pillar arrays without EUV; SIS supplies fluorine-free etch selectivity (silicon-containing BCPs would need CF4).

title: Stencil-indexed deposition builds the 3D staircase, replacing trim-etch loops
idea: Substitute the staircase made by dozens of resist-trim + oxide/nitride fluorocarbon etch loops with deposition-defined steps: sputter an oxide-semiconductor/Mo/Al2O3 tier stack through a stepper-indexed stencil whose aperture edges move inward ~0.5 um per tier at each staircase site, so every tier terminates at its own offset; stencils are swapped and stripped in oxalic acid/H2O2.
why: 3D DRAM staircase cost (fact 2): eliminates ~N/2 litho-trim-etch cycles and all their fluorocarbon use; staircase becomes native to deposition.

title: Crystal-plane KOH trenches on (110) silicon replace plasma deep etch
idea: Substitute fluorocarbon/Bosch deep etching with crystallographic wet etching: on (110) Si, KOH/TMAH etches trenches bounded by vertical {111} planes at AR >100:1 with atomically smooth walls; a dedicated bonded (110) capacitor wafer carries fin-shaped trench plates lined with TiCl4-ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN, its SiN hard mask opened with hot H3PO4.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): crystalline AR >100 from a wet bench costing ~1/20 of a HAR etcher, no fluorinated chemistry; line-shaped plates resist the pillar leaning that limits AR today.

title: Area-selective ALD replaces deposit-then-etch for tier dielectrics
idea: Substitute 'deposit everywhere, then etch' with area-selective ALD: small-molecule inhibitors (acetylacetone, aminosilanes, or alkanethiol monolayers on metal) block nucleation on a tier's metal/semiconductor faces so Al2O3/ZrO2 grows only on dielectric faces (and vice versa for Mo), self-aligning each tier's isolation and capacitor dielectric with no dielectric etch.
why: Removes fluorocarbon dielectric etches and the overlay error that blocks dense 4F² (fact 4); each self-aligned step deletes a litho+etch pair.

title: Catalyst-grown vertical nanowire transistors replace etched 4F² pillars
idea: Substitute etched Si pillars for vertical 4F² access transistors with bottom-up nanowires: Sn or Al catalyst dots placed by block-copolymer templating grow single-crystal Si nanowires (SiH4, Au-free) from bitline seeds, with in-situ B2H6/PH3 switching n+/p/n+ along the growth axis to form source/channel/drain without implants.
why: 4F² vertical-channel cell without high-AR Si etch or fluorinated gases; abrupt in-situ junctions shrink the leakage tail (fact 3); non-gold catalysts avoid deep-level traps.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous TiN sponge replaces smooth capacitor electrodes
idea: Substitute the smooth storage-node TiN with a nanoporous one: ALD a TiN/AlN nanolaminate electrode (TiCl4/TMA/NH3), selectively leach the Al phase in dilute NaOH/TMAH to leave a 3D sponge with 5-10 nm ligaments, then conformally coat with ALD ZrO2 and top TiN.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): 2-3x electrode area in the same pillar (Cs 5 -> 10+ fF) without raising AR; no HF needed.

title: Peroxide-soluble germanium tiers replace SiGe sacrificial layers
idea: Substitute SiGe sacrificial tiers (normally released with HF/H2O2/acetic or CF4 remote plasma) with Ge-rich tiers (sputtered a-Ge in deposited oxide-semiconductor stacks, thin strained Si0.3Ge0.7 in epi stacks) that dissolve in warm dilute H2O2 as soluble GeO2, selectivity to Si >100:1, opening lateral cavities for capacitors and gate-all-around access devices.
why: Water-based release for 3D DRAM lateral devices (fact 2); higher selectivity permits thinner sacrificial tiers, so more tiers per um of stack.

title: Selective SiGe oxidation converts sacrificial tiers into stacked buried oxides
idea: Substitute etch-and-fill tier isolation with in-place conversion: oxidize a Si/SiGe superlattice from its slit sidewalls at 750-850 C, where SiGe oxidizes 5-20x faster than Si, so each SiGe tier becomes buried insulator and the stack becomes multi-tier SOI; a thin Si:C barrier on each Si tier blocks rejected Ge from the channels.
why: Isolates stacked single-crystal channels (fact 2) without HF or fluorocarbon dielectric etch; fully depleted SOI body per tier tightens the leakage tail (fact 3).

title: One CZ donor wafer supplies twenty tiers via repeated layer splitting
idea: Substitute 'one CZ wafer per device layer' with 'one CZ donor per ~20 layers': H/He co-implant a donor, bond to the growing stack, split at ~400 C, restore the donor with touch CMP and H2 anneal (no HF), re-implant; each transferred 50-200 nm single-crystal Si layer becomes a partially pre-processed array tier.
why: Quartz-crucible chokepoint (Spruce Pine >80%): CZ wafers per bit fall 10-20x for stacked tiers; single-crystal tiers beat deposited channels on leakage tail.

title: Infrared through-silicon optical links replace Bosch-etched copper TSVs
idea: Substitute SF6/C4F8 Bosch-etched Cu TSVs with vertical free-space optics: silicon is transparent at 1310 nm, so beams from bonded InP micro-emitters (Cl2/BCl3-etched) on the base die cross 30 um-thin DRAM dies to Ge-on-Si detectors (GeH4 epi) placed at a unique XY site on each die (position multiplexing).
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): no via keep-out zones or via yield loss, which drive much of the 3x area per bit, and the stack is built with no fluorinated deep-etch gases.

title: Water-droplet self-alignment with alkylsilane rings replaces precision die placement
idea: Substitute high-precision pick-and-place for die-to-wafer DRAM stacking with capillary self-alignment: a water droplet on each hydrophilic bond site pulls the coarsely dropped die into ~0.2 um registration, the surrounding hydrophobic ring made from octadecyltrichlorosilane or plasma-polymerized HMDSO instead of the usual fluorinated FDTS.
why: Stacking capital and throughput (fact 6): parallel, tool-light alignment for thousands of dies per minute, enabling finer hybrid-bond pitch per dollar.

title: Bonded diamond spreader tiers replace silicon spacers under stacked DRAM
idea: Substitute passive silicon spacers in memory-on-logic stacks with bonded polycrystalline CVD diamond tiers (CH4/H2 growth, mechanical thinning, O2-plasma activation, laser-drilled Cu vias) between GPU and stacked DRAM, spreading heat ~10x better than Si so DRAM can sit directly on compute.
why: Data movement (fact 5): DRAM-on-logic cuts ~3-4 pJ/bit (HBM) to <0.5; diamond keeps DRAM <85 C so refresh rate does not double (fact 3); no fluorinated coolants.

title: Carbon-mandrel, titania-alumina spacers replace fluorocarbon quadruple patterning
idea: Substitute oxide-spacer/fluorocarbon SAQP with an ashable/chlorinable set: amorphous-carbon mandrels (O2 ash), ALD TiO2 first spacers and ALD Al2O3 second spacers etched with Cl2/BCl3 at >20:1 mutual selectivity, printed with a non-fluorinated PAG (sulfonium camphorsulfonate) resist, so ~16 nm pitch uses only O2, Cl2, BCl3 and HBr.
why: Litho capital and fluorine dependence (fact 4): ArF + SAQP array lines without EUV, fluorocarbon spacer etches, or PFAS photoacid generators.

title: Fluorine-free DRAM flow certification as a U.S. permitting fast lane
idea: Create a U.S. 'fluorine-free memory' track: CHIPS/DoD funding and EPA permitting priority for DRAM lines that use no F-gases or PFAS (built from epi stacks + Cl/Br etch + Mo-chloride + AAO/drawn-glass capacitors), with defense/hyperscaler offtake; the fab skips F-GHG point-of-use abatement and PFAS wastewater treatment.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: est. 12-24 months faster permitting, a few % lower capex, immunity to PFAS bans/supplier exits and to the fluorspar chokepoint (China ~60%+).
